newsitem.title: USA: U.S. CREDIT MARKET OUTLOOK -- Q3 GDP to dominate.
newsitem.headline: U.S. CREDIT MARKET OUTLOOK -- Q3 GDP to dominate.

text.p: Credit markets will focus on their first glimpse of third quarter Gross Domestic Product (GDP) on Wednesday, although any market reaction could be muted as Friday's all-important jobs data approaches.
GDP growth, due at 0830 EST/1330 GMT, is expected to have risen 1.8 percent rate in the third quarter, well below the second quarter's 4.7 percent blistering pace.
"(The data) could either stop the rally in its tracks, or keep it going another day," said Michael Cloherty, money market economist at R.H. Wrightson & Associates.
Bond prices jumped two points on Tuesday, bringing the 30-year bond yield to a six-month low of 6.68 percent.
Market participants said it is unlikely the rally will continue that significantly, since the October employment report is due on Friday.
"Additional gains will be limited. The focus is on Friday," said Michelle Laughlin, chief Treasury market strategist at Prudential Securities Inc.
She added that the headline number isn't the main attraction.
"There is more focus on real final sales. All the growth in the third quarter was in inventories, but how much inventories is the question," Laughlin said.

"So, the larger the (headline) print, the better for the market because most likely it will be due to a larger inventory gain," she said, noting that final sales needs to be below a one percent gain to be bullish for the bond market.
Still, Tuesday's big gains limits any upside move, analysts said, noting there is a bigger risk the market will selloff, although it's doubtful a selloff would wipeout Tuesday's big gains.

Meanwhile, the Federal Reserve releases its Biege Book report at 1200 EST/1700 GMT. Market participants do not expect any major market reaction. Some noted that the market is mainly interested in wage portion, but the smaller than expected 0.6 percent rise in the third quarter Employment Cost Index tempered any market inflation worries.
New home sales for September are due at 1000 EST/1400 GMT. The market is looking for a big decline after a big jump in August. But, a market reaction is unlikely, economists said.
Traders also cited a dollar recovery versus the yen and falling commodities prices as bullish items. -- 212-859-1660
